newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Frontline to move to Bermuda.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Frontline to move to Bermuda.

text.p: Swedish shipping group Frontline said on Tuesday that it planned to move to Bermuda, partly for tax reasons.
"The move is expected to mean annual cost savings of around 25 million crowns as of 1998," the company said in a statement.
The transfer would also mean lower taxes and it would be a way to avoid demands that the group's crews have Swedish wage agreements, it said.
To facilitate the move, Frontline's main owner, Hemen Holding B.V., will propose to other shareholders that Frontline AB transfer its operations to the newly created company Frontline Ltd on Bermuda.
Shareholders are offered to swap one share in Frontline AB for a newly issued share in Frontline Ltd, it said.

"The main aim with the presented proposal is to increase the company's competitiveness and to strengthen its profile and get a chance to attract capital on the international market," the company said.
Frontline will seek a listing on the Oslo Stock Exchange in Norway -- expecting its share to start trading there around July 4 -- and later in New York.
Frontline's proposal to leave Sweden comes after a recent argument between Swedish telecoms giant Ericsson and the Social Democratic government about the Swedish business climate.
Ericsson's chief executive, Lars Ramqvist, has said the company board is looking into moving group headquarters abroad because of the poor Swedish business climate and high taxes for individuals.
